entry.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research. AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research.
entry.summary:
AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: What Does Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning Really Improve in LLM Agents?
entry.summary:
While multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning (RL) excels on long-horizon tasks, its performance gains remain highly sensitive to interaction constraints. Evaluating across sampling breadth K and interaction depth T via Pass@(K,T), we show that trajectory-level RL advantages depend on sufficient turn budgets, diminishing significantly when budgets tighten. Besides, agentic RL does not uniformly elevate single-step decision quality; rather, its strength concentrates in error recovery and long-horizon resilience.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #reinforcement-learning

entry.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games. Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games.
entry.summary:
Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Aggregate-Surplus Maximizing Monetary Policy -- by David Baqaee, Ariel Burstein, Joao Guerreiro
entry.summary:
We study optimal monetary policy in a general heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian (HANK) economy. Instead of maximizing a social welfare function, the policymaker maximizes the joint surplus of all households, without taking a stance on how that surplus should be distributed. This is the policy that maximizes resources left over if winners from reform were to compensate losers.

Source: NBER Working Papers (National Bureau of Economic Research) · Tags: #macroeconomics #econometrics #distributed-systems #agents

entry.title: Limited knowledge exchange across biological subfields in agent-based modelling: an LLM-assisted bibliometric analysis
entry.summary:
Agent-based models (ABMs) are widely used across the biological sciences. While applications differ between biological subfields, the mathematical and statistical methods underlying ABMs largely do not, raising the question of how much knowledge is exchanged between subfields. We address this question by developing a bibliometric pipeline that combines a database keyword search with coarse- and fine-grained classification by a large language model (LLM).

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #databases #agents

entry.title: Competitive Equilibrium for Linear Chores is CLS-complete. The competitive equilibrium (CE) is a fundamental concept for markets, with applications to efficient and fair allocation of resources.
entry.summary:
The competitive equilibrium (CE) is a fundamental concept for markets, with applications to efficient and fair allocation of resources. We consider the fundamental question of computing a CE in the most basic Fisher market model where agents have linear preferences. While it is known that we can compute a CE in strongly polynomial time with linear goods, there is no known polynomial-time algorithm for CE with linear chores.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #algorithms #agents
